newsitem.title: ROMANIA: IMF to visit Bucharest - PM designate.
newsitem.headline: IMF to visit Bucharest - PM designate.

text.p: Romania's credibility in the West has been enhanced by reformist Emil Constantinescu's presidential election victory, with an IMF delegation due to visit next week, the country's prime minister designate said.

Victor Ciorbea, currently mayor of Bucharest, said in an interview on Wednesday evening that the International Monetary Fund had sought the talks immediately after Constantinescu defeated ex-Communist Ion Iliescu last weekend.

"We will have the chance to learn of the demands of the International Monetary Fund. Let's hope the outgoing government will provide us with the documents to ascertain the exact situation of the Romanian economy," he said.
"The essential changes brought about by the elections will...provide the credibility necessary for a real dialogue with the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank and other institutions."

The IMF concluded a $280 million credit programme with Romania last December, but it suspended payments earlier this year, citing restrictions on the country's foreign exchange market. Romanian economists also said the IMF was unhappy with other aspects of post-Communist reforms.
Central Bank governor Mugur Isarescu said in an interview this week that Romania had every reason to hope for restoration of the credits.

Constantinescu's centrist Democratic Convention, which threw ex-communists out of government in general elections this month, campaigned on a programme blending tighter financial discipline with improved benefits for the disadvantaged. --Ron Popeski, Bucharest newsroom +401 312-0264
